# visualtone — LLM authoring guide

Music = colored curves over time. Audio is a pure function of curve data.

## Axes
- t (seconds): time / x
- y (MIDI float 0–127): pitch
- size (0–1): gain / stroke width
- hue (0–360°): timbre family (ring of synth anchors)
- lightness (0–1): brightness → spectral tilt + filter cutoff (default 0.5). Cutoff = fundamental × 1.5·32^lightness (cap 18 kHz): 0.3 ≈ 4.4×, 0.5 ≈ 8.5×, 0.7 ≈ 17×, 0.9 ≈ 34×. Stabs/leads need ~0.6+ to reach the 2–6 kHz presence band.
- saturation (0–1, optional): 1 = pure tone, lower = more noise ("grey = noisy")

## Curve syntax (points)
Optional per point:
- ease: step | linear | in | out | inOut | exp — how to **arrive** at this point
- tween: seconds — only the last `tween` seconds before this point interpolate

Defaults when ease omitted:
- size 0 → >0: step (instant attack)
- size falling: exp
- both size 0: silence between
- pitch while sounding: linear (legato); use silence between notes for staccato

## Notes shorthand
```json
{ "t": 0, "y": 36, "size": 0.9, "duration": 0.15, "ease": "exp" }
```
- hold (default): sustain then ~20ms release
- exp: exponential decay over duration (drums, hats)

## Hue families
0° kick, 30° bass, 70° pluck, 110° bell/keys, 160° supersaw lead, 210° pad, 260° vocal, 300° snare/clap, 335° hi-hat

## Track FX (optional)
- `channel`: `0` or `[0,1]` stereo route from one mono curve
- `space`: hall reverb send 0–1 (visual: glow). Shared stereo FDN, not a per-track reverb. The hall input is highpassed at 120 Hz so bass notes do not leave a low rumble.
- `room`: short room send 0–1, a second shared bus (`master.room`)
- `echo`: delay send 0–1
- `release`: tail after the note curve, milliseconds. 0 (default) is a hard cut.
- `chorus`: `{ "depth": 0.4, "rateHz": 0.4, "mix": 0.35 }` — 3 modulated delays after the track comp
- `duck`: `{ "by": "kick-drum", "amount": 0.6 }`
- `timbre`: partial override of internal synth vector
  - `velocity` 0–1: louder notes open the filter (`cutoff *= 2^(velocity*(size-0.7)*2)`), quieter notes darken it. 0 = off.
  - `drift` 0–1: slow per-voice pitch drift (±6 cents × drift), per-onset cutoff jitter, random unison phase. Seeded, so renders stay reproducible. 0 does not touch the noise sequence.
- `bpm` + `master`: `{ "loudness": -14, "saturation": 0.3, "reverb": { "size": 0.7, "decay": 0.6, "preDelayMs": 25, "damping": 0.4, "width": 0.85 }, "room": { "size": 0.4, "decay": 0.3, "preDelayMs": 8 }, "delay": { "beats": 0.75 }, "eq": { "highShelf": { "freq": 8000, "gain": 2 } }, "comp": { "threshold": -9, "ratio": 2 }, "limiter": { "ceiling": -1, "releaseMs": 60 } }`
  - Master chain: sum → `eq` → `saturation` (even harmonics + DC block, skipped at 0) → `comp` → drive → loudness match → lookahead limiter (always on, 5 ms lookahead, ceiling -1 dBFS, also watches 4× intersample peaks). Raising `loudness` makes the limiter work harder and lowers the peak-to-loudness ratio.
  - `reverb.damping` is how fast highs die in the tail. `preDelayMs` defaults to 25 on the hall and 8 on the room.
- Mono tracks on `channel: 0` play in the LEFT speaker only when the score is stereo; put kick/bass on `[0,1]` to center them.

## Mixing / modulation / groove (optional)
- `eq`: `{ lowCut, highCut, lowShelf: {freq, gain}, highShelf: {freq, gain}, peaks: [{freq, gain, q}] }` (Hz, dB)
- `comp`: `{ threshold: -18, ratio: 3, attackMs: 10, releaseMs: 120, knee: 6, makeup: 0 }`
- `lfo`: `[{ target: lightness|pitch|gain|pan, depth, rate (Hz) | beats (period), shape: sine|triangle|saw|square, phase }]`
  - lightness depth = ±brightness offset; pitch depth = ±semitones; gain depth = dip 0–1; pan +1 = right
- `automation`: `{ lightness: [{t, v}], gain: [{t, v}] }` — linear; lightness v is an offset, gain v a multiplier
- score `swing` 0–1 (1 = triplet), `swingGrid` 8|16; track `swing` overrides
- `humanize`: `{ timeMs, size }` deterministic jitter per note
- Mix tips: pads quiet (size ~0.1–0.15 when sustained), lowCut everything except kick/bass, duck pads/stabs by kick.

## Output
CLI `--bit-depth 16|24|32f` (16 default with TPDF dither), `--no-dither`.

See examples/rising-pad.json

## Example: stereo sketch
See examples/stereo-sketch.json

## Example: groove (120 BPM, A minor, notes + points)
See examples/demo-groove.json

See examples/deep-house-v5.json (generated by examples/scripts/deep-house-v5.mjs)

See examples/deep-house-v6.json (generated by examples/scripts/deep-house-v6.mjs). Tuned with `analyze --profile deep-house` until it had no findings.

## Example: deep house v7 (same arrangement, wetter and less mechanical)
See examples/deep-house-v7.json (generated by examples/scripts/deep-house-v7.mjs). Adds a pure sub plus a saturated mid bass, a keys layer, `release` on stabs and keys, hall and room sends, `timbre.velocity` / `timbre.drift`, chorus, and `master.saturation`. Tuned until `analyze --profile deep-house` reported no findings. Replacing the old per-track reverb changes any older score that uses `space`; previously rendered WAVs are unchanged.

## Clips (external audio)

TTS stays outside visualtone. Render WAV, then:

```json
{ "id": "voice", "role": "voice", "clip": { "src": "tts/scene2.wav", "at": 3.2, "gain": 1, "fadeIn": 0.05, "fadeOut": 0.08, "trim": [0, 4.1] } }
```

`clips` is the same shape as an array. The library does not read files: pass decoded audio as `render(score, { clips: { "tts/scene2.wav": { sampleRate, buffers, sha256 } } })`. The CLI loads paths relative to the score and records sha256 on `result.inputs` and on the analysis report.

Duck a bed under speech: `{ "by": "voice", "amount": 0.5, "holdMs": 80, "releaseMs": 280, "band": [1000, 4000] }`. `band` ducks only that range with `out = x − (1−g)·bandpass(x)` (0 dB-peak RBJ bandpass, f0 = √(f1·f2), Q = f0/(f2−f1)); the center gain equals the duck gain. `holdMs` stops the music pumping between words.

## Sound effects

A track `sfx` array expands into curve tracks (`role: "sfx"`, ids like `fx:whoosh-0`) before render.

| name | use | params |
|------|-----|--------|
| whoosh | transition | `direction` -1..1 (pan travel), `brightness`, `duration`, `pan`, `size` |
| riser | build into a cut | `duration`, `brightness`, `size` |
| swell | soft entrance | `duration`, `brightness`, `size`, `pitch` or `y` |
| impact | hit | `low` 0..1 (boom amount), `tail` seconds, `size`, `brightness` |
| pop | UI click | `pitch`/`y`, `brightness`, `size` |
| tick | small mark | `brightness`, `size` |
| key | single bell note | `pitch`/`y`, `duration`, `size` |
| shimmer | sparkle tail | `duration`, `brightness`, `size`, `pitch`/`y` |

```json
{ "id": "fx", "sfx": [{ "sfx": "whoosh", "t": 4.0, "duration": 0.4, "size": 0.7, "direction": 0.6 }] }
```

## Segments

`mix([{ score, at, fadeIn, fadeOut, prefix }], master)` places each score on the outer timeline. Groove runs in segment-local time before the shift. A segment `master` is ignored (warning); the argument wins. JSON form, loaded by the CLI: `{ "segments": [{ "src": "scene2.json", "at": 4.0, "fadeIn": 0.2, "prefix": "s2/" }] }`.

Track `offset` shifts one track. Track `seed` keeps noise stable when tracks are reordered.

## Picture data

`render(score, { envelopes: { fps: 30 } })` returns `envelopes.tracks[id].onsets` (seconds) and `.level` (RMS per frame, after the strip and duck, before sends). Frame i covers `[i/fps, (i+1)/fps)`. `envelopes.master.level` is after the limiter. CLI: `--envelopes env.json --fps 30`.

## Musical spelling

With `bpm` (and optional `meter`, default `[4, 4]`): point/note `at: "4:2"` (bar 4, beat 2, 1-based), `pitch: "A3"`, note `len: "1/8"`. Missing bpm is an error. `chord("Am7", "A3")` and `pattern("x...x..x", { bpm, y, bar, step })` are functions, not schema.

## Instruments by synthesis method

`"instrument": "cello"` sets engine and hue together. Do not set `engine` or `hue` on the same track. Instruments that share a generation method and a parameter set share one model:

- additive / `harmonic` (engines bow, brass, reed, bass): violin, viola, cello, contrabass, electric-bass, trumpet, horn, trombone, tuba, saxophone, oboe, bassoon
- additive / `drawbar` (organ): organ, organ-full
- modal / `bar` (marimba): marimba, xylophone, vibraphone, glockenspiel
- modal / `membrane` (drum): kick, tom, snare, conga, frame-drum
- modal / `stiff-string` (piano): piano
- modal / `plate` (cymbal): hihat-closed, hihat-open, crash
- waveguide / `plucked-string` (pluck): steel-guitar, nylon-guitar, harp
- waveguide / `blown-bore` (wind): flute, clarinet
- fm / `two-operator` (epiano): electric-piano
- subtractive / `virtual-analog` (sub): sub-bass, reese-bass, offbeat-bass
- wavetable / `hue-ring` (wavetable): synth-pluck, synth-lead, synth-pad

The four `harmonic` engine names now run one generator (`createHarmonic`) with a preset per instrument (`HARMONIC_PRESETS`). Output matches the earlier separate engines to 1.4e-14. `INSTRUMENTS` and `MODELS` are exported with each instrument's model, engine, hue, and reference recording set. Not built yet: source-filter voice and choir, stochastic particle percussion (clap, shaker), electric guitar on the plucked-string waveguide.

## Acoustic engines

`engine`: `wavetable` (default) | `pluck` (Karplus–Strong) | `marimba` (modal bar) | `epiano` (FM) | `organ` (drawbar additive) | `drum` (modal membrane) | `wind` (flute or clarinet bore) | `bow` (bowed string) | `piano` (struck string) | `brass` (lip reed) | `bass` (contrabass or electric bass) | `sub` (electronic bass) | `reed` (oboe or bassoon) | `cymbal` (hi-hat or crash). The acoustic engines are polyphonic: overlapping notes are not cut. Hue does not interpolate with the wavetable ring.

`pluck` is a Karplus–Strong string with a fractional delay. The loop length compensates the averaging filter and the dispersion allpass, so high notes stay in tune. Hue 0°–139° is a steel guitar, 140°–279° nylon, 280°–360° harp. A harp is plucked nearer the center, rings longer, and is lowpassed on the way out. `size` moves a guitar pluck toward the bridge; `lightness` lengthens the ring. Body resonances sit at 118 Hz, 150 Hz, and 220 Hz.

`drum` is a circular membrane: mode ratios are the Bessel zeros. Hue 0°–44° kick (a short beater pitch drop), 45°–139° tom, 140°–229° snare (membrane plus snare noise), 230°–309° conga, 310°–360° frame drum. Higher pitches decay faster. `size` excites the upper modes and the beater; a soft hit stays dark. `lightness` near 1 is a center strike. The beater is lowpassed, and the kick is lower still, so the hit is a thud; snare wires are filtered on their own. Pitch can go down to 20 Hz.

`wind` is a blown bore. Hue 0°–179° is a flute: open pipe, one-period delay. The jet saturation is odd, so even harmonics are added inside the loop; a hard note brings the octave up near the fundamental, and high notes use less loop loss. Hue 180°–360° is a clarinet: closed pipe, half-period delay and a sign flip, so the bore is odd. Chalumeau stays nearly a sine; above the break an octave is mixed in after the bore, and in the altissimo that octave can pass the fundamental. A soft note is darker and speaks more slowly. An odd saturation feeds the loop, and the zero crossings stay on the delay, so the pitch stays on the note. `size` raises the breath and opens the loop filter. A highpass inside the flute loop stops DC from growing until the jet saturates and the note dies. The pitch drifts by a few cents, as a player's does. Loudness is modulated after the bore, with irregular motion from 8 to 20 Hz: about −35 dB on the flute and −33 dB on the clarinet.

`brass` is a lip reed: harmonics whose slope opens with loudness. Hue 0°–89° trumpet, 90°–179° horn (high notes stay darker even when loud), 180°–239° trombone, 240°–299° tuba, 300°–360° saxophone. Partial phases are spread so a bright spectrum does not line up into a sawtooth corner. A bell resonance sits at a different frequency for each instrument. `size` flattens the spectrum and adds a little noise. Pitch drifts by about 1.5 cents (tuba 3). Held notes also move in level at 8–20 Hz: about −30 dB on trumpet, −32 on horn, −38 on trombone, −26 on tuba, and −42 on saxophone.

`bass` is a low string. Hue 0°–179° is a bowed contrabass. A broad body sits near 100 Hz, and a dense set of narrow peaks is looked up from each partial’s instantaneous frequency, so the partials do not rise and fall together. Vibrato is slower, 4.5 Hz, about ±6 cents on low notes and ±5 cents once the pitch is high, and the depth wanders a little from cycle to cycle. Held notes also have about −31 dB of 8–20 Hz level motion. After the bow lifts, a low note rings for about 0.8 s and a high note for about 0.3 s, longer when the note is soft. Bow noise sits between the partials. Hue 180°–360° is an electric bass fitted to NSynth: the string decays while held (about 1.4 s at 55 Hz, faster when the note or the partial is higher) and a finger transient dies within a few dozen milliseconds. Pitch can go down to about 28 Hz.

`sub` is an electronic dance bass. Hue 0°–119° is a sub: near a sine, with a pitch dip of about 4 semitones that settles onto the note. `size` squares the wave and opens the lowpass, so a harder note is brighter. Hue 120°–239° is a reese: two saws about 8–15 cents apart, then a lowpass. Hue 240°–360° is a rhythmic bass: level and lowpass both fall while the key is held, so a 16th grid has accents. Pitch can go down to about 27 Hz. Duck the track from the kick so the low end clears on each hit.

`reed` is a double reed. Hue 0°–179° is an oboe, nasal formant near 1500 Hz. Hue 180°–360° is a bassoon, formant near 540 Hz. A conical bore has every harmonic. `size` opens the spectrum. Pitch drifts by about 1.5 cents. Held notes move in level at 8–20 Hz: about −32 dB on the oboe and −31 dB on the bassoon.

`cymbal` is unpitched metal. Hue 0°–119° closed hi-hat, 120°–199° open hi-hat, 200°–360° crash. Midi chooses the plate size: a higher note is smaller and brighter. Releasing a closed hat chokes it.

`bow` is Helmholtz motion of a bowed string, built from exponentially sloped harmonics. Partial phases are spread so a brighter slope does not line up into a sawtooth corner. Hue 0°–119° violin, 120°–239° viola, 240°–360° cello. `size` slows the spectral rolloff and opens the lowpass in front of the body resonance. After about 0.2 s the player leans into vibrato. The rate stays near one value, the depth follows pitch, and both wander a little each cycle: violin 5.4 Hz, about ±17 cents low and ±6 cents high; viola 5.4 Hz, about ±3 cents low and ±12 cents high; cello 5.2 Hz, about ±4 cents low and ±19 cents high. The vibrato does not lift every partial together. A seeded body table, a few hundred narrow peaks plus the older broad modes, is looked up from each partial’s instantaneous frequency every 32 samples, so the partials rise and fall on their own. A separate irregular 8–20 Hz motion sits on top: about −31 dB on violin, −26 dB on viola, and −24 dB on cello. The tail after the bow lifts follows pitch and loudness: about 0.3–0.7 s on violin, 0.5–1 s on viola, and about 0.9 s low to 0.2 s high on cello, longer on a soft note. Bow noise is added after the body filter so it fills the gaps between partials.

`piano` is a struck string. Partials sit at `n·√(1+B·n²)`. B rises with pitch, about 0.00009 at C2 and about 0.002 at C6. Higher notes and higher partials die sooner. A second string is detuned by about 0.7 cents. `size` hardens the hammer so upper partials are louder and hang longer. Hue toward 360° darkens the hammer. A quiet soundboard noise decays with the string.

`marimba` hue selects the bar: 0°–119° marimba (modes 1, 3.92, 10.08, 15.8), 120°–199° xylophone, 200°–279° vibraphone (slow tremolo), 280°–360° glockenspiel. Decay time shortens as pitch rises; the glockenspiel shortens more slowly, so the high bars still ring. Upper modes open with strike^1.4, so a soft hit stays near a sine, and only the longest marimba bars add the mode near 10×. A short mallet knock sits on the attack. While held, the bar rings at its own rate; `release` is the damping after note-off.

`organ` uses the nine drawbars (16′, 5⅓′, 8′, 4′, 2⅔′, 2′, 1⅗′, 1⅓′, 1′). Hue 0° and 360° are a stopped flute (8′ plus odd partials), 180° is the full mixture, with an open flute in between. Longer pipes speak more slowly. `size` and `lightness` open the upper stops, so a harder note is brighter as well as louder. `release` (default 180 ms) is the time to about −60 dB. The 16′ stop stays under the 8′ so the key you play is the pitch you hear. No Leslie yet, so pitch stays steady. While held, the whole rank moves together by about −30 dB at 8–20 Hz.

A wavetable note no longer steps to zero when the curve reaches silence. The 2 ms gain smoother finishes first (that step was a click on every held note). `release` is an additional tail on top of that fade.

## Voiceover profile

`analyze --profile voiceover-bed`. Set track `role` to `voice`, `sfx`, or `music`. Checks: music yields 1–4 kHz while the voice is active, sfx does not mask the music, sfx is not too dense. Band shares and warmth count only `role: "music"` tracks, and suggestions name those track ids. `master.lufs` is a BS.1770 target and replaces the RMS `master.loudness` match when set; `render().master.loudnessDb` and the CLI line then report the measured LUFS. Default `sampleRate` is 48000; existing examples that write 44100 stay 44100.

## Static pan

Track `pan` is -1..1 (0 = center, equal-power). `automation.pan` is an offset added to it, so a whoosh can travel. `automation.lightness` stays an offset and `automation.gain` stays a multiplier.

## Listening loop
The way to hear a render without ears: render, analyze, read the PNG, edit the score from findings, diff.

1. `npx visualtone analyze score.json --profile deep-house --json report.json --png report.png`
   - `.json` renders with stems (masking + per-track share). `.wav` is mix-only (16/24 PCM, 32-bit float).
   - `--panel spectrogram|curves|stems|bands|loudness|phase|kick|masking|ssm|space|dynamics` writes one panel.
   - Texture metrics (json scores only): `warmth` is the 150–500 Hz share. `space.wetShare` is hall+room+delay bus energy over dry stems plus those buses (needs a score render, not a wav). `space.tailRatioDb` is the median tail-vs-attack level. `dynamics.hitVariationDb` is the 25th percentile of per-track local hit-level deviation (tracks with at least 16 hits; a section fade is not counted). `dynamics.repetition` is the fraction of bar pairs 4 or 8 bars apart with similarity above 0.98. `stereo.bandSideMidDb` splits side/mid into low, mid, and high.
2. Read `report.json` findings first. Each has `severity`, `message`, `suggestion` naming a score field (`channel`, `size`, `eq.peaks`, `automation.gain`, `master.comp`, `room`, `release`, `timbre.velocity`, `timbre.drift`, `humanize.size`).
3. Built-in profiles: `deep-house`, `techno`, `pop-edm`, `ambient`, `voiceover-bed`. Numbers are mixing experience, not a standard. `npx visualtone profile ref.wav -o my.json` builds one from references (do not commit the wav).
4. `npx visualtone diff before.json after.json` lists metric deltas and which findings appeared or went away.
5. Optional taste log, one JSON object per line in `feedback/ratings.jsonl`:
   `{"date":"2026-10-06","file":"examples/deep-house-v5.json","reportHash":"…","scores":{"groove":4,"timbre":3,"clarity":4,"overall":3},"note":""}`
   Scores are 1–5. Do not invent a rating the user did not give.

What the pictures show: score curves (pitch vs time), log spectrogram, one row per stem, band shares, short-term LUFS, phase scatter, kick envelope, masking matrix, self-similarity + chroma, space (bus wet bars and the tail curve), dynamics (one dot per hit; a straight row is a mechanical part).

## Timbre measurement

For tuning one instrument, not a mix.

- `npx visualtone timbre note.wav --midi 60 [--ref ref.wav] [--json out.json]` measures one note: f0 and cents, pitch stability, glide, vibrato, and the cents left after drift and vibrato are removed; attack 10–90%, decay dB/s (overall, early, late), T60, release after `--note-off`, envelope modulation from 8 to 20 Hz in dB (faster than vibrato); partials 1–16 in dB, slope dB/oct, odd/even, inharmonicity B (f_n = n·f0·√(1+B·n²)), HNR, spurious peaks off the partial series (aliasing), per-partial decay for 1–8, and how much each partial wanders on its own; also how far partials 1–12 move with the vibrato and whether they move together, how jagged partials 1–20 are, the noise between harmonic lines, and the highest partial still above that noise; centroid, flatness, log-mel, MFCC, and how many ms the high partials lag the low ones; clicks, DC, NaN. A score input renders first; `--track id` picks a stem.
- With `--ref`, `compareTimbre` scores each metric against a tolerance (error ≤ 1 passes) and turns the misses into findings, worst first. The reference must be a single note at the same pitch, 44.1 kHz or more.
- `npx visualtone probe track.json [--pitches 36,48,60,72,84] [--sizes 0.3,0.6,0.9] [--note 1.5] [--tail 2] [--ref dir] [--wav probe.wav]` plays one track template over a pitch × size grid and measures the dry stem. Findings check habits most acoustic instruments share: in tune, louder and brighter with size, higher notes decay sooner, no clicks. Reference files are named `60.wav` or `60_0.9.wav`.
- The ceiling for that comparison is a recording, not a GM soundfont. `node scripts/fetch-references.mjs` downloads single notes from TinySOL (Ircam, CC BY 4.0: flute, clarinet, oboe, bassoon, violin, viola, cello, contrabass, trumpet, horn, trombone, tuba, saxophone), VSCO 2 Community Edition (CC0: marimba, xylophone, glockenspiel, harp, organ, kick, snare, conga, timpani), and Salamander Grand Piano V3 (Yamaha C5, CC BY 3.0). `node scripts/compare-references.mjs` writes `references/gap.json`. WAV files stay out of git. Distance 0 matches the recording; each metric error is capped at 3. `node scripts/measure-floor.mjs` writes `references/floor.json`: the median error between two TinySOL takes of the same violin or cello note on different strings (404 pairs). Harmonic balance has a floor of 3.90 and pitch 1.66, so real takes already disagree there. Shimmer (8–20 Hz) has a floor of 0.36. Comparison divides each error by max(1, that floor). When a recording is below 48 kHz the render is resampled to that rate first, so both sides are measured in the same band. `excess` now also includes vibrato-locked partial motion, whether partials move together, harmonic-ladder jaggedness, noise between the lines, and cycle-to-cycle vibrato irregularity. `excessV1` keeps only the previous metrics, so an untouched preset can be compared with the old number. Mean excess over the floor: flute 1.31, clarinet 1.56, oboe 1.50, bassoon 1.53, trumpet 1.49, horn 1.50, trombone 1.28, tuba 1.47, saxophone 1.46, organ 1.52, violin 1.28, viola 1.27, cello 1.29, contrabass 1.34, piano 1.81, marimba 1.76, xylophone 1.51, harp 2.03, glockenspiel 2.05, vibraphone 1.99, electric piano 1.96, electric bass 1.42, kick 2.02, snare 2.18, conga 1.64, timpani 2.09. The same sets as excessV1: flute 1.31, clarinet 1.57, oboe 1.40, bassoon 1.40, trumpet 1.46, horn 1.45, trombone 1.13, tuba 1.45, saxophone 1.37, organ 1.38, violin 1.35, viola 1.32, cello 1.30, contrabass 1.39, piano 1.77, marimba 1.71, xylophone 1.48, harp 2.00, glockenspiel 2.07, vibraphone 1.95, electric piano 1.91, electric bass 1.36, kick 2.04, snare 2.18, conga 1.72, timpani 2.17. A value of 1 is about as far apart as two real takes. Shimmer (8–20 Hz) for each sustained set is in the same report: violin, trombone, organ, and electric piano sit within about 1 dB of the recording; viola, cello, and contrabass sit about 4–6 dB away; tuba, bassoon, horn, and vibraphone sit further apart. Nylon guitar and cymbals have no recorded reference yet. Electric bass is scored against NSynth (Engel et al. 2017, CC BY 4.0): `node scripts/fetch-nsynth.mjs` keeps dry electronic-bass notes from the valid and test archives (MIDI 28–57, velocities 50/100/127). The two splits share three instruments and no notes, so the fit uses valid and holds out test pitches. Renders are resampled to the recording's 16 kHz before scoring. `node scripts/fit-preset.mjs electric-bass nsynth-electric-bass` writes `references/fit/electric-bass.json`. Mean excess over the floor: 2.12 before, 1.37 on the fit split, 1.34 on the held-out pitches. Two real basses at the same pitch and velocity sit 1.73 apart, so the fitted preset is closer to each recording than the recordings are to each other. The same rule fits every other recorded instrument. Sustained notes get an estimated release where the mid-note level drops about 6 dB; that `hold` is stored on each catalog note, and both comparison and fitting measure only the held portion. TinySOL notes were filled out to about six pitches at pp/mf/ff where the archive has them. The highest pitch, at every dynamic, is the test split; the rest is the fit split. Bar, stopped-flute organ, piano, harp, flute, clarinet, and timpani numbers now live in named presets, the same shape as `HARMONIC_PRESETS`. Before any search, those hues matched the previous samples. `node scripts/fit-preset.mjs <instrument> <set>` searches mean excess with a fixed seed and 4 workers, penalizing cents above 8 and any click, and writes `references/fit/<instrument>.json`. A preset is copied back only when holdout excess falls by at least 0.005 and the probes stay clean. A bowed-string pass then matched the spectrogram: vibrato depth follows pitch, and violin and cello keep a few fixed body modes. Landed holdout excess on the old ruler: violin 1.48→1.27, viola 1.44→1.35, cello 1.71→1.48, contrabass 1.76→1.42, trombone 1.21→1.14, saxophone 1.53→1.42, flute 1.27→1.20, xylophone 2.05→1.52, harp 1.98→1.82, piano 2.17→2.15, timpani 2.37→2.31, organ 1.47→1.40. A later bowed-string pass replaces that fixed ladder with a dense body looked up from each partial’s instantaneous frequency, and the vibrato no longer lifts every partial together. Holdout excess on the new ruler: violin 1.13, viola 1.16, cello 1.25, contrabass 1.40. Full-set excess / excessV1: violin 1.28 / 1.35, viola 1.27 / 1.32, cello 1.29 / 1.30, contrabass 1.34 / 1.39. Vibraphone uses dry NSynth `mallet_acoustic_056` notes; `node scripts/fetch-nsynth-set.mjs` takes valid and test only, and its holdout is 1.94→1.81. Electric piano was searched on three dry `keyboard` + `electronic` instruments and the holdout moved 1.88→1.77, but clicks on one probe note went from 1 to 2, so that preset stays at the previous numbers. Clarinet’s holdout moved 1.51→1.46, but at MIDI 60 a loud note was darker than a soft one, so the brightness probe failed and that preset stays too. Trumpet, horn, tuba, oboe, bassoon, marimba, and glockenspiel did not improve on the holdout, so those presets stay at the previous numbers. The search reports remain in `references/fit/`. Electronic bass, wavetable voices, and cymbals have no recording of that instrument. Kick, snare, and conga each have a single recording, so they are not searched. Steel guitar, nylon guitar, and frame-drum hues stay sample-identical. WAV files stay out of git. If a sample map’s labeled pitch is at least six semitones away from the recording, the comparison uses the pitch the recording actually plays.
- Library: `analyzeNote(buffer, sampleRate, { start, stop, noteOff, midi })`, `compareTimbre(ours, ref)`, `probeTrack(track, opts)`, `analyzeProbe(mono, sampleRate, cells)`.

CLI: `npx visualtone render score.json -o out.wav`
Schema: `npx visualtone schema`
